newsitem.title: MEXICO: One killed as hurricane slams into Baja California.
newsitem.headline: One killed as hurricane slams into Baja California.

text.p: Hurricane Fausto ploughed through the southern tip of Mexico's Baja California on Friday, killing a U.S. tourist, ripping off roofs and downing power lines and trees as winds reached 120 mph (195 kph), officials said.

An American tourist in the resort town of Cabo San Lucas who attempted to ride out the storm in a trailer park was electrocuted when a light post fell onto his trailer, the government news agency Notimex said.
Erick Hite, 26, of San Diego, was killed in the San Jose del Cabo-Cabo San Lucas corridor, Notimex said, citing South Baja California governor Guillermo Mercado Romero.
In La Paz, the streets were littered with debris after the hurricane passed through, witnesses said.
Mexico's National Meteorological Services said in a report that the hurricane had crossed into the Gulf of California and was headed toward the Mexican mainland at Sinaloa state.
Much of South Baja California state lacked power, and highways were rendered impassable by flooding, witnesses said.

"The hurricane is passing through La Paz in this very moment with winds of about 140 kph (87 mph)" Guillermo Salgada, the state interior minister, said in an interview. "The worst is over as winds were about 195 kph (120 mph) earlier."
The meteorological service said the storm was a Category 1 hurricane, the weakest on a scale of 1 to 5.
Hundreds of residents were taking refuge in schools and other public places as the state government arranged evacuations ahead of time, Salgado said.

Juan Valdez Sanchez, a state superintendent of the Federal Electricity Commission, told Notimex strong winds knocked down many power lines throughout much of the state, cutting off electricity which he said would be restored on Saturday.
